behavioral_notes.observation: The module turns every res.partner into a publishable website document. By inheriting website.seo.metadata it gains SEO meta fields, and it adds is_published (tracking=True), website_description (Html, sanitize_overridable, html_translate) and website_short_description (Text, translatable). The related website_published field and the publish toggle come from website.published.mixin (website/models/mixins.py: website_published is a Boolean related='is_published'; website_url is a computed Char with a 'View on website' button). So a back-office contact becomes a front-end profile purely by flipping is_published -- a publishing semantic invisible from the bare schema.

_compute_website_url() calls super() then, for any persisted partner, overrides website_url to '/partners/%s' % ir.http._slug(partner). This wires the generic website.published.mixin redirect button (registered as the website_redirect_button widget on the contact form, see res_partner_views.xml) to the public detail route, so editors jump from the contact form straight to the rendered public page. The slug embeds the partner id + a human-readable display-name segment.

The public detail route is deliberately NON-semantic (raw <partner_id> string, not a model converter) because it browses with sudo()/SUPERUSER_ID. It _unslug()s the id, sudo-browses the partner, and renders 'website_partner.partner_page' ONLY if the partner exists AND (partner.website_published OR the visitor has website.group_website_restricted_editor); otherwise raise request.not_found(). It also canonicalises the URL: if the recomputed slug differs from the requested one it redirects to the canonical /partners/<slug> (SEO de-duplication). This published-or-editor access gate is the security boundary for the whole public profile, enforced in code, not via ir.rule.

Because is_published has tracking=True, _track_subtype() is overridden so that toggling publication posts a dedicated mail.message.subtype in the contact chatter: website_partner.mt_partner_published when turned on, mt_partner_unpublished when turned off (both defined noupdate in data/website_partner_data.xml). A pure data change (publish flag) thus produces an audit/social side-effect in mail -- a cross-model effect not derivable from field metadata. The same data file force-publishes base.main_partner so the company profile is live out of the box.

behavioral_notes.element: partner_page / partner_detail QWeb templates as the shared, extensible base page
behavioral_notes.observation: This module owns only the skeleton: partner_page wraps website.layout with two oe_structure editable drop-zones ('DROP BUILDING BLOCKS HERE TO MAKE THEM AVAILABLE ACROSS ALL PARTNERS') and t-calls partner_detail. partner_detail renders the image, a schema.org Organization microdata block, a contact widget (address/website/phone/email) and website_description, and crucially exposes empty left_column / right_column slots. Downstream modules extend THIS base by xpath-inheriting partner_detail and t-set-ing those slots: website_customer fills implemented_by_block / references_block; website_crm_partner_assign adds grade/reseller blocks plus the /partners listing and /partners/grade/.../country/... faceted routes and its own _get_partners_response; event reuses the same published-partner profile. website_partner itself ships no listing route -- only the detail page -- making it the minimal shared base the channel/customer/event apps build on.

behavioral_notes.element: frontend (no own OWL/JS; reuses website builder)
behavioral_notes.observation: extract_frontend reports present=false: zero JS files, zero OWL components, zero asset bundles, zero registry adds of its own. The editing UX (drag-and-drop snippets into the oe_structure zones, the publish toggle widget) is entirely inherited from the parent website module's client-side builder; this module contributes only server-side QWeb templates and the is_published form widget reference. All interactivity is borrowed, not defined here.

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: value_model is network (Stabell & Fjeldstad mediating technology), inherited from and consistent with its parent website: this module extends the web platform that mediates between the organization and an open population of visitors, here by exposing res.partner records as public profile pages. Its worth is mediating-and-infrastructure -- it connects visitors to partners (resellers, customers, event organizers) and provides the shared, reusable /partners/<id> page that downstream channel/customer/event modules plug into; value grows with the number of published partners and consuming apps, the hallmark of a network rather than a sequential transformation (chain) or a problem-solving cycle (shop). activity_class is support (NOT primary, unlike the parent website): website_partner is a thin, application:false base library -- a single inherited model, one detail route, no listing, no own UX. It does not itself deliver the market presence; it provisions a shared publishing capability that the truly customer-facing modules (website_crm_partner_assign reseller directory, website_customer references, event) build their primary service upon. apqc_category 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services because publishing partners/channel members as public web profiles is a demand-side marketing/channel-publishing activity (promoting the partner network and channel ecosystem to the market); 13.0 Develop and Manage Business Capabilities was considered (it is reusable enabling infrastructure) but rejected because the artifact produced -- an outward-facing marketing profile page in the website channel -- is squarely market-and-sell content, not an internal capability-management asset.
classification.apqc_alternative_considered: 13.0 Develop and Manage Business Capabilities (reusable enabling base) -- rejected: output is outward-facing marketing/channel content, so 3.0 fits the delivered value.
